name: Hong Kong
summary: A British colony from 1841 (Hong Kong Island), enlarged in 1860 and 1898; returned to China in 1997 as a Special Administrative Region under “one country, two systems”, with its own flag, laws and currency.

knownFor.label: Victoria Harbour skyline
knownFor.note: One of the densest skylines in the world.

knownFor.label: Hong Kong cinema
knownFor.note: Bruce Lee, Jackie Chan, Wong Kar-wai.

location.value: Southern China, on the eastern side of the Pearl River estuary; about 1,110 km².

terrain.value: Hilly to mountainous with little flat land: Hong Kong Island, the Kowloon Peninsula and the New Territories.

climate.value: Humid subtropical, with typhoons in summer.

resources.value: Few natural resources, but the deep, sheltered waters of Victoria Harbour.

disasters.value: Typhoons, most often in summer, sometimes causing floods or landslides.

urbanisation.value: The fourth-most densely populated region in the world.

migration.value: Refugees came from mainland China, especially after 1949; over half a million people left in 1987–1996 before the handover.

economicBase.value: Finance, shipping and services; manufacturing gave way to services in the 1980s.

tradeRoutes.value: A major commercial port; the world's ninth-largest exporter and eighth-largest importer.

wealth.value: One of the highest per capita incomes in the world.

moneyAndTax.value: The Hong Kong dollar, held by a currency peg; low taxes.

inequality.value: The world's most expensive housing market and severe income inequality.

governmentType.value: British crown colony under a governor until 1997; since then a Special Administrative Region of China.

keyRulers.value: Governors such as Murray MacLehose; Chief Executives since 1997.

succession.value: The Chief Executive is appointed by China's State Council after nomination by a 1,500-member Election Committee.

institutions.value: The Basic Law is its constitution; its courts follow the common law tradition from British rule.

armyAndTech.value: The People's Liberation Army's Hong Kong Garrison is responsible for defence.

majorWars.value: The First Opium War, after which the Qing ceded Hong Kong Island; Japanese occupation (1941–1945).

territoryChange.value: Kowloon added (1860); New Territories leased for 99 years (1898).

alliancesRivals.value: China's central government handles defence and diplomacy; Hong Kong keeps its own economic and cultural ties abroad.

inventions.value: No notable inventions listed. A leading finance and logistics centre: third-ranked global financial centre and busiest airport for international cargo.

openness.value: A free port with low taxes and almost no trade controls.

communicationTransport.value: The MTR rail network, the Star Ferry and the world's seventh-busiest container port.

religion.value: Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism have the most followers, then Christianity and Islam.

languageWriting.value: Chinese and English are official; Cantonese is spoken by 93.7% of people.

artsArchitecture.value: Colonial buildings, and more skyscrapers than any other city.

socialStructure.value: About 91.6% Chinese (2021), mostly from Cantonese and other southern Chinese groups.

sharedIdentity.value: Most people are ethnically Chinese, but Hong Kong has developed a distinct identity.

dailyLife.value: Cantonese food with rice as the staple; cha chaan teng cafés serve local versions of Western food.

neighbours.value: Shenzhen (mainland China) to the north; Macau 60 km to the west.

ideasReligions.value: Traditional Chinese values blended with Western ideals such as economic liberty and the rule of law.

riseSignals.value: British forces took control in 1841, and Hong Kong became a British colony.

peakPeriod.value: Fast growth: GDP rose about 180 times between 1961 and 1997.

declineSignals.value: After the 2020 national security law and the 2021 electoral changes, the pro-democracy camp lost all its seats in the Legislative Council.

outcome.value: Handed over to China in 1997, which guaranteed its economic and political systems for 50 years.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
